mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) relative to the previous quarter signals strong consumer demand, which drives higher corporate earnings expectations and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when RSAFS growth is positive, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) rises above 4.5% for two consecutive months, it signals a tightening monetary policy that reduces liquidity and increases discount rates, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5%, the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances, or the Rank IC for the signal is negative over a 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) and increase in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) signals a strong labor market, which boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint condition of declining UNRATE and rising PAYEMS fails to produce positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of cases, or the Rank IC for the interaction signal is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of high consumer confidence (measured by RSAFS growth exceeding 0.5% monthly), strong demand for goods and services leads to elevated corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When RSAFS growth exceeds 0.5%, the S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of cases, or the Rank IC for the signal is below 0.03 over a 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above 2.5% annually signals persistent inflation, which typically leads to a monetary policy response that compresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when CPIAUCSL annual inflation exceeds 2.5%, or the Rank IC for the signal is negative over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 4.5% for two consecutive months, it indicates a tight labor market that may lead to wage pressures and reduced corporate profit margins, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When UNRATE falls below 4.5%, the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances, or the Rank IC for the signal is below 0.03 over a 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of active monetary tightening (FEDFUNDS > 4.0% and rising), the S&P 500 typically experiences negative returns over the next 60 trading days due to reduced liquidity and higher discount rates.
failure_condition: When FEDFUNDS is above 4.0% and rising, the S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of cases, or the Rank IC for the signal is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts (HOUST) and industrial production (INDPRO) signals robust economic activity, which drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint condition of rising HOUST and INDPRO fails to produce positive 5-day returns in more than 50% of cases, or the Rank IC for the interaction signal is below 0.03 over a 2-year rolling window.
